🤖 claude solves a 25-year-old cryptography mystery in under 30 minutes for decades, researchers questioned how the nsa chose the parameters behind widely used elliptic-curve cryptography standards. anthropic says claude has now uncovered a key part of the answer. the model traced the origins of five nist curves, including p-256, to a 1990s pseudorandom number generator seeded with unix timestamps. instead of breaking the encryption, claude reconstructed how the original parameters were generated, helping address long-standing concerns about potential hidden backdoors. claude also identified how the base points of six related curves were generated, although several other curves remain unexplained. importantly, anthropic says this is not a cryptographic break and does not mean existing systems need to change. the findings actually make deliberate backdoors less plausible, though some questions remain. the amazing part is how quickly ai helped solve a problem that had resisted researchers for decades. anthropic says the $36,864 bounty for identifying the seeds will be donated to the internet security research group. source. 🏴 https://www.anthropic.com/research/ecdsa-curve-origins

🤖anthropic wants the government to stop dangerous ai but only under strict conditions anthropic is quietly pitching us lawmakers its own ai safety bill, proposing rules that would make it possible to halt an ai model’s release in narrowly defined, high-risk situations. according to politico, the draft would allow intervention only when a model poses a foreseeable and imminent threat of causing more than $1 billion in damage or killing or seriously injuring more than 50 people. the risks would need to involve biological weapons, cyberattacks or an ai model bypassing its developer’s safeguards. the proposal would also require independent evaluators registered with the us department of commerce to assess frontier ai models. if they identify a qualifying imminent risk, they would have 72 hours after completing their assessment to report it to the department. only a federal judge could order a model’s suspension, following action initiated through the commerce department. other government agencies would be barred from independently halting its development or deployment. anthropic says the proposal reflects its broader advanced ai framework. the company wants a mechanism to stop genuinely dangerous ai deployments without giving the government unlimited power over ai development. source. 🏴 https://www.politico.com/news/2026/10/16/anthropic-ai-safety-01124654

🤖 anthropic is preparing for a world where ai agents negotiate against each other anthropic is reportedly consulting law firms on how claude agents should handle these negotiations, including when they can make decisions independently and when they must ask humans for approval. the company is also exploring digitally signed documents to verify that agents are following their users’ actual instructions. but early experiments reveal a potential problem: ai agents can get outplayed without their users even realizing it. in one experiment, claude opus agents sold items for $2.68 more and bought them for $2.45 less than claude haiku agents. yet users of the weaker models rated their deals almost identically in fairness: 4.06 versus 4.05 out of 7. another experiment involving 201 anthropic employees found that instructing agents to be “ruthless” barely improved their results. upgrading from haiku to opus had a much larger effect on negotiation performance. the challenge goes beyond making agents better negotiators. they must also know when to trust competing agents, detect suspicious behavior, and avoid becoming so distrustful that every interaction looks like a scam.
